finding.claim: OS command injection in the unauthenticated GET /ping route: req.query.host is concatenated into a shell string passed to child_process.exec, letting any network client run arbitrary commands as the Node process user and read the output.
finding.source: req.query.host on GET /ping (tools.js:6-7), reachable from the network because app.listen(3001) binds all interfaces (tools.js:28).
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, which runs the string via /bin/sh -c.

trace.note: app.listen(3001) with no host argument binds all interfaces, so the route is network-reachable.
GET /ping handler registered with no auth middleware.
req.query.host concatenated into the ping command string without validation.
exec interprets shell metacharacters such as ; | && $() in the injected value.
stdout (attacker command output) returned to the client via res.send(out).

finding.guards_checked: No authentication or authorization middleware on /ping. No validation, allowlist, or format check on host. No typeof check: array or object query values are coerced by concatenation and remain injectable. execFile with an argument array is used only on /version (tools.js:16), not /ping. No loopback-only bind in code; network restriction depends on deployment and is not in the repo. Reproduction: curl -s "http://<host>:3001/ping?host=127.0.0.1;id" and look for uid= in the response. Fix: execFile("ping", ["-c","1",host]) with strict IP/hostname validation and a string type check, add authentication, bind to 127.0.0.1 unless public access is intended. Validation tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: none. tools.js:6 registers /ping with no auth middleware; tools.js:7 concatenates req.query.host into the exec string with no validation, type check, or allowlist; tools.js:28 app.listen(3001) has no host argument so it binds all interfaces. execFile with an argument array is used only on /version (tools.js:16), not on /ping.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: tools.js:7 passes unvalidated req.query.host into exec, which runs through /bin/sh, and tools.js:11 returns stdout to the client, while tools.js:28 binds the port on all interfaces with no auth at tools.js:6, so an anonymous network attacker can inject shell commands and read the output.

finding.claim: Unauthenticated disclosure of host state: GET /version returns the git HEAD commit hash and GET /uptime returns uptime and load averages to any network client. Reconnaissance and fingerprinting aid only; no direct compromise.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated network client reaching GET /version (tools.js:15) or GET /uptime (tools.js:24) on the public listener at tools.js:28.
finding.sink: Response of git rev-parse HEAD via res.send(out.trim()) at tools.js:20, and uptime output via res.send(out) at tools.js:25.

trace.note: Public bind on all interfaces at port 3001.
git commit hash returned to the client.
uptime output returned to the client; err is ignored, so out may be empty on failure.

finding.guards_checked: No authentication on either route. Neither route is injectable: /version uses execFile with a fixed argument array and /uptime runs a fixed command string with no user input. Fix: require authentication on these routes or serve them only from a loopback listener.

verdict.reason: Every trace line matches: app.listen(3001) at tools.js:28 has no host argument, so it binds on all interfaces; /version at line 15 and /uptime at line 24 have no auth middleware; line 20 returns the git HEAD hash via res.send(out.trim()); line 25 returns uptime output with err ignored. An anonymous network client can reach both routes, and no check at tools.js:15-26 blocks them.
